public_rationale: A study published September 7, 2023 found fabricated citations in 55% of GPT-3.5 citations and 18% of GPT-4 citations on its literature-review tasks [e3]. A preprint revised November 7, 2024 reported factual precision of 90.8% for GPT-3.5-Turbo and 91.7% for GPT-4-Turbo, alongside larger gains in factual recall [e4]. Its GPT-3.5 comparator was a January 2024 snapshot [e4]. These studies show task-specific improvements and differing changes in precision and coverage, but neither supplies a matched comparison of launch-era ChatGPT and November 2024 systems across factuality and reliability [e3, e4]. They therefore do not settle whether improvement over the claimed period was substantively small [e3, e4].
limitations: Neither study establishes aggregate progress from November 2022 to November 2024 across representative factuality and reliability tasks.
Citation fabrication, factual precision and factual coverage measure different aspects of performance.
The evidence does not settle practical trustworthiness or define how much improvement would count as substantial.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Two years after ChatGPT came out, on factuality and reliability, which he calls the most important question, we are still pretty much where we were at its release: wishing and hoping.

statement.excerpt: Two years on, on the most important question of all – factuality and reliability — we are still pretty much where we were when ChatGPT first came out: wishing and hoping.

from_speaker: still pretty much where we were when ChatGPT first came out
our_interpretation: The ordinary empirical reading is that factuality and reliability had improved little in substance since ChatGPT's launch.
The comparison runs from the November 2022 launch to the November 2024 post.
Calling factuality the most important question is a value judgment and is not graded.
Continued hallucinations alone cannot establish little improvement.
Pretty much supplies no numerical threshold. Treating this as a claim about unchanged error rates rather than continued need for verification materially affects the assessment.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations of launch-era ChatGPT and November 2024 systems show little substantive improvement across relevant factuality and reliability tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evaluations establish substantial improvements across relevant factuality and reliability tasks between those endpoints.

evidence.explanation: A paired study of literature reviews across 42 topics found substantially fewer fabricated citations with GPT-4. This weighs against a sweeping no-progress reading, but does not compare the actual November 2022 and November 2024 systems.

On matched prompts, GPT-4-Turbo scored 95.0 versus GPT-3.5-Turbo's 79.6 on F1@64, while factual precision was 91.7% versus 90.8%. The different signals matter, and the GPT-3.5 model was the January 2024 version, not launch-day ChatGPT.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Matched evaluations of an archived November 2022 ChatGPT baseline and November 2024 systems across representative tasks, reporting precision, coverage, abstention and serious errors separately, with an explicit standard for substantive improvement.
